stories.title: Comal County begins work on $8.75 million mental health facility
stories.summary: Comal County is building a 16,000-square-foot facility to house an extended observation unit and a crisis residential unit. Funded by the American Rescue Plan Act, the project aims to provide accessible crisis services and reduce reliance on emergency departments. The facility is located in New Braunfels.

stories.title: Marina apartment complex to provide housing for vulnerable residents
stories.summary: Interim Inc. has broken ground on the Marina Kai, a 23-unit studio apartment complex in Monterey County. The project is designed to provide permanent and transitional housing for adults experiencing homelessness and serious mental illness. The developer describes the project as a way to improve everyone's lives.

stories.title: NAMI faces potential eviction from St. Tammany Parish campus
stories.summary: The National Alliance on Mental Illness is negotiating with St. Tammany Parish leaders to remain on the Safe Haven Campus in Mandeville. Parish officials are reportedly asking the organization to pay $160,000 annually to continue operating its day center. Peers currently receiving services have expressed concern regarding the potential move.

stories.title: Psychiatric nurse practitioner outlines seasonal affective disorder signs
stories.summary: Bethanne Carson of Lake Area Psychiatry says seasonal affective disorder is a type of depression that typically begins in late fall or early winter. Symptoms can include fatigue, sadness, and loss of interest in activities. The condition generally eases as spring arrives, according to the psychiatric nurse practitioner.

stories.title: University of Louisiana at Lafayette hosts Mental Health Week
stories.summary: The University of Louisiana at Lafayette is holding a series of events for Mental Health Week, including a resource fair and yoga sessions. The school is also promoting a scholarship for students facing mental health challenges. The university's official message for the week is You Are Not Alone.

stories.title: Mental health app may help unemployed people find jobs, six-week trial suggests - Phys.org
stories.summary: 🛡️ Just a quick check We’re checking your connection to prevent automated abuse Mental health app may help unemployed people find jobs, six-week trial suggests Phys.org The full piece is for subscribers, and the headline is all that is public for now.

stories.title: Tippie College of Business receives $3.5 million for mental health
stories.summary: The University of Iowa’s Tippie College of Business has secured $3.5 million in endowment funding for Tippie Thrive. The peer-led program uses a preventative approach to connect students with mental health resources. The funding will cover ongoing costs to maintain the program's proactive methods for reaching students.

stories.title: Illinois lawmakers call for better prison mental healthcare
stories.summary: State lawmakers are seeking improvements to mental healthcare in Illinois prisons following reports of abuse and poor conditions at the Joliet Treatment Center. Nearly half of the state's prison population is currently on a mental health caseload. Department of Corrections leaders say they are committed to ensuring care.

stories.title: Analysis identifies escitalopram as effective for relapse prevention
stories.summary: A study of nearly 10,000 patients found that the antidepressant escitalopram performed best at preventing depression relapse over a one-year period. Agomelatine and duloxetine followed in effectiveness. Experts note that these findings do not mean all patients should switch medications, as various antidepressants can be effective for different individuals.

stories.title: Study links online sports betting to increased medication use
stories.summary: Researchers at Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health found that states with legalized online sports betting saw a 5% to 7% increase in prescriptions for anti-anxiety and antidepressant medications. The study analyzed a national dataset of employer-sponsored health insurance claims to identify the trend.

stories.title: Film screening addresses teen suicide and mental health
stories.summary: The Kids Mental Health Foundation is hosting a screening of Shattered Ice, a film about a high school hockey team dealing with a teammate's suicide. Psychologist Dr. John Ackerman, who consulted on the script, will join a panel discussion to discuss warning signs and how to start difficult conversations.

stories.title: Heartland Family Service opens crisis center in Papillion
stories.summary: Heartland Family Service has opened a crisis center in Papillion for adults aged 19 and older. The facility is funded by Region 6 and provides immediate mental health treatment for a variety of issues. Staff report seeing individuals dealing with a wide range of personal and emotional challenges.

stories.title: Systematic review suggests mindfulness may improve sleep quality
stories.summary: A meta-analysis of ten randomized trials involving 638 university students indicates that mindfulness interventions can improve subjective sleep quality. Researchers from Shandong Sport University noted that substantial statistical inconsistency and methodological limitations in the existing literature mean the findings should be interpreted with caution.

stories.title: Study finds 45 days of yoga linked to improved mood
stories.summary: A randomized controlled trial in Pune, India, found that 45 days of standardized yoga sessions were associated with better mood scores and sleep quality among 139 healthy adults. Participants, aged 18 to 55, had no prior yoga experience. The results were published in the journal Scientific Reports.

stories.title: Researchers examine brain connectivity changes after yoga
stories.summary: A study published in Scientific Reports investigated how a 45-day yoga routine affects brain connectivity and mood. Researchers combined fMRI brain scans with memory and mood tests to determine if postures, breathing, and meditation could alter how brain regions communicate. The study focused on healthy adult participants.

stories.title: Elisha Goldstein discusses mindful breathing as meditation anchor
stories.summary: Elisha Goldstein suggests that mindful breathing serves as a foundation for meditation because the breath is always available as an anchor to the present moment. The practice involves awareness of the breath in the nose, chest, or belly without any need to manipulate or analyze the process.

stories.title: Adapted mindfulness therapy shows potential for self-harm reduction
stories.summary: Clinical psychologists observed significant reductions in non-suicidal self-injury among outpatients with borderline personality disorder following a nine-week mindfulness intervention. The exploratory study, published in Borderline Personality Disorder and Emotion Dysregulation, tracked participants between 2019 and 2023. The intervention also correlated with increased trait mindfulness.

stories.title: Vagus nerve stimulation studied as mindfulness aid for addiction
stories.summary: A randomized clinical trial published in BMC Medicine suggests that combining mindfulness meditation with transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation may improve inhibitory control in men with alcohol use disorder. The study indicates that targeting brain-heart interplay could be a pathway for developing more effective clinical interventions.

stories.title: AI support linked to worse mental health outcomes
stories.summary: A JED Foundation report finds students using AI for companionship or emotional support report higher rates of anxiety, depression, and loneliness. The study notes that students often turn to the technology when feeling overwhelmed or lacking human connection. The software is available when people are not.

stories.title: OpenAI launches Teen Mode for ChatGPT
stories.summary: OpenAI has introduced Teen Mode for users under 18, a year after a lawsuit alleged the platform contributed to a teenager's suicide. The industry has long contested claims that its products cause harm. The release is a tacit acknowledgment of the company's role in user well-being.

stories.title: Kashmir medical students report late-night sleep patterns
stories.summary: A local study of medical students in Kashmir found two-thirds go to bed after midnight. Researchers cite irregular routines, digital exposure, and stress as factors undermining sleep quality. For many, the day now begins when the lights go out.

stories.title: Artificial light disrupts circadian rhythms
stories.summary: Michigan State University researchers found that one hour of midday daylight exposure restored daily rhythms in grass rats living under office lighting. Humans spend much of their time indoors under artificial light, which differs from the natural cycles around which our biological clocks evolved.

stories.title: Restless legs syndrome linked to perinatal depression
stories.summary: Pregnant women with restless legs syndrome are three times more likely to develop perinatal depression, according to new research. The association is strongest during the third trimester. Investigators suggest screening for the sleep disorder may help identify those at elevated risk for earlier intervention.

stories.title: Sleep apnea severity and COVID-19 outcomes
stories.summary: A retrospective study in BMC Pulmonary Medicine found that initial correlations between sleep apnea severity and complicated COVID-19 courses weakened after multivariable adjustment. The research examined hospital records to determine how sleep apnea relates to clinical outcomes for patients infected with the virus.

stories.title: Exercise linked to lower sleep apnea risk
stories.summary: A study of over 93,000 UK Biobank participants suggests that replacing sedentary time with moderate-to-vigorous physical activity is associated with a lower incidence of sleep apnea. Because time is finite, increasing physical activity inevitably displaces other behaviors, such as sitting still.

stories.title: Brain region links sleep quality to Alzheimer's markers
stories.summary: A study in Alzheimer’s Research and Therapy identifies the locus coeruleus as a potential neurobiological bridge between sleep disturbances and Alzheimer's progression. Dysfunction in this brainstem region is associated with circadian instability in individuals with elevated plasma biomarkers for the disease.

stories.title: Deep sleep changes may signal preclinical Alzheimer's
stories.summary: Research published in Alzheimer’s Research and Therapy suggests that changes in brain wave shapes during deep sleep may serve as non-invasive biomarkers for Alzheimer's disease. These abnormalities appear before memory problems begin. Sleep disturbances are common in those developing the condition.

stories.title: Late-night smartphone use reduces teen sleep
stories.summary: A study of 425 teenagers found that each additional 30 minutes of phone use after 10 p.m. was associated with falling asleep 65 minutes later. Participants who used their phones more than usual after 10 p.m. slept about 20 minutes less on average.

stories.title: Sleep loss increases susceptibility to phishing
stories.summary: A University of California, Irvine study found that click rates on simulated phishing emails rose by 13 percent on the Monday following the start of daylight saving time. Researchers suggest that better sleep likely leads to better decisions when evaluating digital security threats.

stories.title: Fitness industry zone two training gains traction
stories.summary: Zone two training, defined as an intensity that allows for full-sentence conversation, is marketed as a way to improve fitness while minimizing injury risk. The approach gained popularity through health podcasts and bestselling books on longevity. It remains a popular way to shuffle.

stories.title: Choir program benefits children after heart surgery
stories.summary: A pilot choir program for children who underwent the Fontan procedure showed improvements in respiratory indicators and emotional well-being. The eight-week study involved 14 patients aged 8 to 16. The program was developed by a children's hospital in collaboration with a university music school.

stories.title: Singing linked to improved lung function in children
stories.summary: A feasibility study from Ann and Robert H. Lurie Children's Hospital reports that choir singing strengthens breathing capacity and decreases anxiety in children born with a single heart ventricle. The intervention combined in-person and online instruction to address physical and psychosocial challenges.

stories.title: Pressure to succeed impacts young athletes
stories.summary: Pediatricians report that dual demands in the classroom and on the field can undermine the mental health of young athletes. While sports can build community, experts emphasize the need for a culture where participants feel comfortable asking for help when the pressure becomes too much.

stories.title: Weight loss drugs and muscle preservation
stories.summary: An Australian study suggests that lifting weights can limit muscle loss in patients using weight loss drugs. Doctors now recommend exercise as a necessary component of the prescription to ensure patients remain strong while dropping weight. The drugs alone do not build muscle.

stories.title: 73-year-old fitness influencer promotes strength training
stories.summary: Christine Hobson, a 73-year-old marathon runner and Guinness World Record holder, has gained an online following by sharing strength workouts. A former headteacher, she began posting videos after her granddaughter introduced her to TikTok. She aims to show that building strength is possible at any age.

stories.title: Isometric yoga studied for chronic fatigue syndrome
stories.summary: A pilot study reports that 12 weeks of recumbent isometric yoga improved orthostatic cardiovascular responses in patients with myalgic encephalomyelitis and chronic fatigue syndrome. The intervention aimed to mitigate symptoms of postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome. The authors emphasize the study's small size.

stories.title: Reducing protein intake may improve longevity
stories.summary: A review of over 350 studies suggests that lower protein intake could slow biological aging and improve metabolic health. While manufacturers currently add protein to everything from cereal to bottled water, researchers indicate that many sedentary adults may be consuming more than they need for their activity levels.

stories.title: UK food regulations fail to flag unhealthy products
stories.summary: Current UK regulatory systems identify only half of processed and ultraprocessed products as unhealthy, according to BMJ Medicine. New models aligned with official dietary guidance classify more than 90 percent of these items as unhealthy. A unified system may offer the best way forward for the country.

stories.title: Breakfast timing linked to mortality risk
stories.summary: A study of 31,000 people shows that the timing of the first meal of the day is related to mortality risk. The risk of death increases by nearly 30 percent if breakfast is eaten after lunch. Scientists are increasingly investigating the link between meal timing and long-term health.

stories.title: Genetic study links dried fruit and cheese to renal health
stories.summary: A Mendelian randomization investigation suggests that higher consumption of dried fruit and cheese is causally associated with a reduced risk of chronic renal failure. The study used genetic variants to evaluate dietary habits, while noting that frequent alcohol intake increases the risk of developing the disease.

stories.title: Coffee consumption linked to gut bacteria diversity
stories.summary: Regular coffee drinkers appear to have a more diverse community of gut bacteria and measurable differences in digestive function, according to a University of Copenhagen study. Coffee contains more than 1,000 bioactive compounds, and its consumption has been linked to a range of potential health benefits.

stories.title: Danish study reveals how coffee affects the gut
stories.summary: Regular coffee consumption not only alters the composition of the gut microbiota but also affects how the intestines function. This is the finding of a new study by the University of Copenhagen, which its authors say could pave the way for new approaches to tackling

stories.title: Ketogenic diet knowledge gaps found in Saudi Arabia
stories.summary: Adults in Saudi Arabia following a ketogenic diet demonstrated an average knowledge score of 58 percent regarding dietary principles and nutritional composition, according to BMC Nutrition. While participants maintained adherence to behaviors, achieving target macronutrient ratios remained a persistent practical difficulty for the surveyed cohort.

stories.title: Regular coffee consumption alters gut bacteria and digestive physiology
stories.summary: If you drink coffee regularly, it appears to alter not only your gut bacteria but also the physiology of the gut itself. That is the conclusion of a study from the University of Copenhagen, which may help point the way towards better treatments for constipation.

stories.title: Longevity supplement trial shows vascular results
stories.summary: A multi-ingredient supplement improved measures of blood vessel health over six months in a small trial at the University of Surrey. The study was supported by the supplement's maker, and researchers emphasize that the trial measured markers of vascular health rather than heart attacks or strokes.

stories.title: Kate Farms founder to launch longevity gummies
stories.summary: Richard Laver is launching a new company named Ian on December 22. The brand features a flagship daily gummy sachet containing 24 ingredients targeting mental clarity, antioxidant defense, and gut health. Each serving contains 10 grams of fiber, 3 grams of sugar, and 40 calories.

stories.title: Clinically proven MonaJuventa Nu for healthy ageing
stories.summary: The healthy ageing and longevity market continues to gain momentum as consumers seek ways to stay active, healthy and more vital for longer. Rather than simply extending lifespan, consumers are increasingly focused on extending their healthspan, maintaining vitality, physical function and overall well-being as they

stories.title: Rapamycin study finds no survival benefit
stories.summary: A retrospective analysis of 11,474 kidney transplant patients found survival rates were nearly identical between those taking rapamycin and those who were not over an 11 year period. The drug remains a popular choice in longevity circles. The data suggests the results are complicated by patient details.

stories.title: Men's Day event to discuss wellbeing in Saldanha
stories.summary: The Better Man Project is hosting a Men's Day event at The Bay Club and Social in Saldanha on 21 November. The programme covers mental resilience, masculinity and financial well-being. It concludes with a screening of the Springboks versus Ireland rugby match for attendees.

stories.title: Maris Dae launches kelp skincare line
stories.summary: Wellness brand Maris Dae has introduced a collection of skincare products derived from Pacific Northwest kelp. The company says its mission is to create clean and non-toxic products that support skin barrier health. The name is inspired by the French word for marine to evoke a sense of sophistication.

stories.title: Luxury wellness sector pivots to preventive health
stories.summary: Hospitality and wellness businesses are shifting toward personalized health assessments and clinical diagnostics, according to executives at the Greater Bay Area Health and Longevity Summit. The industry is moving away from conventional spa experiences to integrate nutrition, stress management and medical testing into travel programs.

stories.title: Aman Group announces Atma wellness brand
stories.summary: Aman Group is launching Atma, a hospitality brand focused on performance living, with tennis player Novak Djokovic as a global partner. The first location is scheduled to open in Miami in 2031. The brand aims to integrate training, recovery and nutrition into luxury hotel stays.

stories.title: Aman Group to open Atma tower in Miami
stories.summary: Aman Group has announced Atma, an ultra-luxury brand centered on wellness and longevity. The first location will be a 1,049-foot tower in Miami, featuring a 120,000-square-foot spa and wellness center. The project is slated for completion in 2031 with interiors designed by Studio Paolo Ferrari.

stories.title: Corinna Maharani marks 25 years of Ayurveda
stories.summary: Corinna Maharani is celebrating 25 years of practicing Ayurveda. The milestone was recently highlighted by the Montecito Journal. The full piece is for subscribers. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: Wellness travel brand partners with Novak Djokovic
stories.summary: A new wellness travel brand is incorporating health tests and laboratory services into its hospitality offerings. The project features a partnership with Novak Djokovic. The full piece is for subscribers.

stories.title: The Ayurveda Experience expands U.S. presence
stories.summary: The Ayurveda Experience is expanding its U.S. operations for its iYURA and Modernica Naturalis brands. The company claims to have 2.3 million customers worldwide and combines traditional herbal preparations with contemporary skincare innovation. It offers personalized product guidance alongside its direct-to-consumer platform.

stories.title: Alvas Ayurveda Hospital hosts Diwali treatment camp
stories.summary: Alvas Ayurveda Hospital has launched an Abhyanga Saptaha treatment camp to coincide with the Diwali festival. The event focuses on traditional Ayurvedic practices. The hospital is located in India and provides various wellness treatments to the public.
